judgements.justification: nDd9 (B) wrongly read the experiments as 15- and 18-dimensional, but QFcb in A made the same error, and nDd9's 4 rests mainly on correct points.
B's chair gave an oral on 4, 7, 7, 8 (mean 6.5) with no reviewer arguing for an oral, citing an 'absolutely above the bar' judgement found in no public review.
B's Reviewer_1UMR gave the only 8 in either committee at confidence 2 on a two-sentence review with no weaknesses, lifting B's ratings toward the oral.
No flaw was disclosed on one forum only; the forest-gap concession answered B's own reviewer and the Algorithm 2 flaw was found by B, not disclosed.
B's ybbQ found a real Algorithm 2 flaw the rebuttal skipped, and nDd9's single-tree versus forest gap was conceded, yet B's meta-review weighed neither and gave an oral.
No score moved after the rebuttal in either committee; eRj1's edit only added that the response satisfied them.

Only B raised the Algorithm 2 flaw, the single-tree theory versus forest experiments, the missing d > 2 theorem and the database-histogram work; only A raised the coordinate swap and the shrinking gain over uniform sampling.
Both committees treated the shared weaknesses (writing, intuition, thin related work) as revision items; the gap came from weighting the novelty, not a weakness.
Neither chair adopted a single reviewer's position; B's tier follows no reviewer.
No reviewer changed a score in response to the other reviews.
The authors skipped ybbQ's Algorithm 2 point, but ybbQ thanked them and kept a 7; nothing shows the omission held that score down.
B's Reviewer_1UMR rated 8 on two sentences, did not check the math, never joined the discussion, and the score counted unchallenged.
Neither chair went below its reviewers' majority; A's poster matches 6, 7, 7.
Neither chair stated a view and then deferred to a score threshold.
nDd9's 4 rests on central points (writing, related work, theory-experiment gap), not a peripheral detail.
Both committees judged the paper as a theoretical coreset contribution with supporting experiments.
No reviewer raised a score on the rebuttal.
Both committees asked the same things of a theory paper; neither imposed an extra requirement.
A's tPz3 and eRj1 misstated the coreset size as near-linear, but that did not raise A's ratings or tier, and B's praise rested on correct claims.
No reviewer acknowledged a resolved main concern while keeping a below-threshold score; eRj1 kept a 7.
Both committees accepted promised revisions (intuition, references); neither refused to credit them.
No reviewer's stated stance diverged from the score.
The off-record 'above the bar' judgement may come from the chair or SAC; nothing shows a late extra reviewer was called in.
No reviewer said the exposition was unclear because the field was outside their expertise against an expert finding it clear.
No reviewer raised a score silently.
B's meta-review does not discount nDd9's 4 for silence; it simply sets a tier the scores do not support.
Neither committee had a detailed, checked champion well above threshold; B's highest score is 1UMR's thin 8.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading at high confidence.
No reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical tradition.
B's meta-review states novelty above the bar but writing 'almost ... unpublishable' and asks for polishing; it argues only for acceptance and gives no case for an oral.
B's reviewers named specific prior work (database histograms, R-trees, Feldman-Langberg) and checked novelty against it, while A's QFcb only noted the missing related-work section without naming it.
B's meta-review does not misstate reviewer positions toward a lower decision; its unsourced quote pushes the other way.
Neither committee raised a narrow-audience concern.
B had a partly misreading detractor but still gave the higher tier; the mechanism runs the other way.
No new experiments were posted on either forum.
Neither chair followed low-confidence scores over a high-confidence expert above them.
No objection was added after the response period.
Rating scales look comparable; A's 6, 7, 7 and B's 7, 7 match similar verbal assessments.
Neither committee judged the headline claim overstated.

reasoning: Committee B gave an oral on lower and more critical ratings (4, 7, 7, 8) than A's poster (6, 7, 7), with a meta-review that calls the writing almost unpublishable and cites an unsourced 'above the bar' novelty judgement. Existing reasons cover this: the chair set the tier above the scores (R02) without a stated case for an award (R30), a thin low-confidence 8 counted (R03, R12), B passed over known flaws such as the Algorithm 2 error and the forest gap (R05), and the two committees saw different issue sets and different depths of prior-work knowledge (R07, R31). The stage 1 candidate of novelty outweighing writing is the chair's own weighting, which R02 covers, so no new reason was added.
